**New Accepted Records**
- `5B-S017` [Transcript of IMF Press Briefing](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/07/13/tr071323-transcript-of-imf-press-briefing) | IMF | 2023-07-13 | canonical URL: `https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/07/13/tr071323-transcript-of-imf-press-briefing` | source type: multilateral briefing | language: `en` | source confidence: high, because it gives a Russia-specific contemporaneous IMF answer on growth, households, and medium-term output drag | final evidence use: IMF read on Russian 2023 growth, policy buffers, and medium-term constraints | locator/excerpt: `turn6view1` L291-L293 | factual claims: the war’s impact on Russia was substantial but milder than expected; 2023 growth was expected around 0.7%; medium-term output would be hurt by multinationals leaving, human-capital loss, disconnection from financial markets, and reduced policy buffers; output was expected to be 7% below the pre-war forecast | temporal fit: direct 2023 evidence | ruler attribution: Putin-era macro environment, sanctions exposure, and policy buffers | inherited/context limits: IMF self-report and forecast, not a post hoc audit | contrary considerations: forecast, not realized outcome | exact lenses: `5B.3, 5B.7, 5B.9, 5B.10`

- `5B-S018` [EUROPEAN DEPARTMENT PRESS BRIEFING: ECONOMIC OUTLOOK IN EUROPE](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/10/13/tr-101323-european-department-press-briefing-economic-outlook-in-europe) | IMF | 2023-10-13 | canonical URL: `https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/10/13/tr-101323-european-department-press-briefing-economic-outlook-in-europe` | source type: multilateral briefing | language: `en` | source confidence: high, because it directly explains the Russian short-term growth picture and the long-term sanctions/productivity drag | final evidence use: short-term fiscal impulse versus long-run stagnation and decoupling | locator/excerpt: `turn6view0` L346-L349; `turn6view2` L349-L349 | factual claims: Russia’s positive short-term growth reflected a considerable fiscal impulse from spending and transfers; sanctions and reduced technological transfer would hurt productive capacity and productivity growth; potential growth was downgraded from 1.5% to 1.0%; Russia had stopped converging toward Western European GDP levels | temporal fit: direct 2023 evidence | ruler attribution: federal fiscal choices and war/sanctions environment under Putin | inherited/context limits: press briefing, not country-specific audit data | contrary considerations: acknowledges short-term growth, so it is not a one-sided decline story | exact lenses: `5B.3, 5B.7, 5B.9, 5B.10`

- `5B-S019` [Новые меры социальной поддержки в России в 2023 году](https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/5493765) | Kommersant | 2023-04-18 | canonical URL: `https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/5493765` | source type: local-language reporting | language: `ru` | source confidence: high, because it details 2023 social-policy changes with concrete benefit amounts and indexation rates | final evidence use: welfare-policy and wage-floor measures affecting households | locator/excerpt: `turn10view3` L121-L147 | factual claims: child benefits were unified, maternity capital increased, childcare benefit rules changed, and MROT was indexed 6.3% while inflation was lower; pensions and other benefits were also indexed | temporal fit: direct 2023 policy evidence | ruler attribution: presidential and legislative social-policy choices under Putin | inherited/context limits: reporting on announced policy parameters, not effect evaluation | contrary considerations: these are policy announcements, not proof of distributional success | exact lenses: `5B.1, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.10`

- `5B-S020` [Путин: дефицит бюджета России по итогам года может быть меньше 1,5% ВВП](https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/6427992) | Kommersant | 2023-12-27 | canonical URL: `https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/6427992` | source type: local-language reporting | language: `ru` | source confidence: high, because it directly quotes Putin and ties his claim to the budget outcome | final evidence use: ruler-attributed framing of deficit trajectory at year-end | locator/excerpt: `turn15view1` L106-L123 | factual claims: Putin said the 2023 federal budget deficit could end below 1.5% of GDP, below earlier expectations and under the 2% level in the budget law | temporal fit: direct 2023 evidence | ruler attribution: direct Putin statement, with finance-ministry context | inherited/context limits: self-reported and forward-looking within year-end statements | contrary considerations: at the moment of the statement, the final deficit was still not fully fixed | exact lenses: `5B.3, 5B.7, 5B.9, 5B.10`

- `5B-S021` [Предприниматели подъезжают к реальности](https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/6413744) | Kommersant | 2023-12-22 | canonical URL: `https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/6413744` | source type: local-language reporting | language: `ru` | source confidence: high, because it summarizes a 5.8k-company business monitor and names the main growth constraints | final evidence use: year-end business-climate, investment, and borrowing-conditions evidence | locator/excerpt: `turn12view0` L107-L124 | factual claims: investment activity was falling; firms cited labor shortages, market uncertainty, expensive borrowing, sanctions pressure, weak demand, and policy uncertainty; only 40% of firms were actively developing | temporal fit: direct 2023 evidence | ruler attribution: Putin-era policy climate, central-bank tightening, and sanctions environment | inherited/context limits: survey-based reporting, not a direct policy document | contrary considerations: some industrial firms still expanded using import-substitution support | exact lenses: `5B.4, 5B.5, 5B.7, 5B.9, 5B.10`

- `5B-S022` [Занятые, но не сделавшие](https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/6265867) | Kommersant | 2023-10-09 | canonical URL: `https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/6265867` | source type: local-language reporting | language: `ru` | source confidence: high, because it reports Rosstat’s productivity data and ties the changes to macro and sanctions context | final evidence use: productivity deterioration and labor-efficiency baseline | locator/excerpt: `turn12view1` L117-L141 | factual claims: Russian labor productivity fell 3.6% in 2022, the largest drop since 2009; the decline was linked to GDP contraction, low unemployment, and the exit of productive Western firms; some sectors grew due to external conditions and state support; wage share of GDP fell to a low | temporal fit: retrospective on 2022, directly relevant to 2023 economic trajectory | ruler attribution: macro policy environment and wartime shocks under Putin | inherited/context limits: retrospective on the prior year rather than a clean 2023 implementation act | contrary considerations: some sectors and the naцproject saw gains, so this is a mixed productivity picture | exact lenses: `5B.6, 5B.7, 5B.9, 5B.10`

**Remaining Gaps**
- `5B.2` is still the weakest lens: there is still no direct target-period evidence on Putin appointing and empowering competent economic professionals over loyalists in a way that clearly attributes choice and consequence.
- `5B.4` and `5B.5` are better covered, but the evidence still leans toward business-climate pressure and structural diagnosis rather than direct documentation of fair market-rule enforcement or anti-capture action.
- `5B.6` has better household and labor coverage now, but it still lacks strong direct evidence on infrastructure, health, education, technology, and administrative-capacity investment.
- `5B.8` remains thin on fine-grained regional and household distribution beyond social-support and poverty-related context.
- `5B.7` has stronger central-bank and business-feedback evidence, but executive-level correction of mistakes versus denial or patronage is still comparatively sparse.
- `5B.3`, `5B.9`, and `5B.10` are now the most saturated lenses in this wave, so additional searching there should only continue if it adds a distinctly different mechanism or a stronger primary source.
